title: Your Agent Might Actually Lie to You
tagline: Three parts on the hackathon build: a Stop hook that will not let a coding agent say done until a real browser agrees.
description: I built GuardianKane for the TestMuAI Kane CLI hackathon, where it placed 2nd. This is the story of that first version: why the gate exists, the four paired experiments that tested it, and what I found when I re-read my own logs and had to ask who checks the checker.
coverAlt: Series cover: Your agent might actually lie to you, with three stacked part tiles: the broken chart, the unasked question, and who checks the checker.

title: GuardianKane: It Will Not Let Your Agent Lie
tagline: Two parts on the full build: the twelve-phase rebuild, and the visual layer that makes verification something you can see.
description: After the hackathon, GuardianKane went from a Stop hook to a reviewed, phased loop with a scope guard, a file lock, a secret scan, and a dashboard of code, memory, and PRD graphs with a chat panel wired into the live Claude Code session. Part 1 is how the rebuild happened and why most of it was wiring. Part 2 is the tour, including the bugs the dashboard exposed in the gate itself.
coverAlt: Series cover: GuardianKane, it will not let your agent lie, with two stacked part tiles: the rebuild, and the visual layer.
